messages:
alex: Heads up — ran the INT8/GPTQ/AWQ bakeoff on H100s with CUDA 15 + TensorRT-LLM today. Seeing a consistent quality delta for AWQ quantized Llama-2-13B: ~2.3% EM drop on our QA set vs fp16 baseline. Latency looks fine but accuracy regression is alarming.

sophia: ugh. did you run the same seed + prompt set? any sign it's a tokenizer mismatch or preprocess? :thinking:

alex: same seed, same prompt set. tokenizer identical. Also saw sporadic kernel warnings in the container logs: `cuBLAS lt GEMM algo - fallback to algo 0` and a lot of `libnvinfer.so` warnings. Pasting truncated logs: ```
[W] TRT: Failed to select kernel for op MatMul with dtype int8, fallback to int32 path
[W] cuBLASLt: algo selection mismatch, trying safe path
```

ryan: that's interesting — we started seeing cuBLASLt fallback behavior after the CUDA15 driver update. TRTLLM recently pulled a change to support fused int8 kernels; on some H100 microcode versions it falls back which can change ordering and tiny numerical diffs. could explain ~2% EM.

maia: also note AWQ's scaling and bias folding assumptions can interact poorly with fused TRT kernels. AWQ expects per-channel scaling applied in a certain op order. If TRT fuses ops differently the quantization noise changes.

ml-ci-bot: build-quant-bakeoff #385 finished: AWQ-int8 on TRTLLM (CUDA15) — accuracy: 0.923, baseline fp16: 0.946, delta: -0.023. Latency +7% for TRT fallback path. Artifacts: s3://redwood-ci/bakeoffs/385/

alex: I also ran the same model with vLLM runtime (CPU+CUDA kernel offload) using our INT8 path — no accuracy drop but seeing intermittent KV cache mismatch after ~2.5k tokens on H100 with driver 535.x. Stack snippet: ```
RuntimeError: KVCache dimension mismatch: expected 1024, got 1008
 at vllm::kv_cache.cc:124
```

ryan: that KV mismatch smells like a memory alignment/padding change in the cuBLASLt path when using blocked GEMMs for int8. Different kernel tiling -> different cached sequence chunking. Have you reproduced with smaller batch or forcing `--no-contiguous-cache`?

alex: repro with `--no-contiguous-cache` stops the crash but brings latency up 18%. Repro steps: ```
./run_bakeoff.sh --model l2-13b --quant awq --runtime trtllm --cuda 15 --driver 535.45 --prompts testset.jsonl --seed 42
```

sophia: try forcing cuBLAS workarounds: `export CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG=:4096:8` and `--tensorrt-precision int8 --tensorrt-force-legacy-kernels`. In one of our earlier runs that changed fusion choices and restored AWQ numbers.

maia: if that fixes accuracy, it's a strong hint TRT kernel fusion/order is the root cause. We should also test with CUDA14 + same TRTLLM build — we had a Fedora image with CUDA14 that didn't show the delta.

alex: quick numbers: AWQ-int8 on TRTLLM (CUDA14): accuracy 0.942 (delta -0.004), on CUDA15: 0.923 (delta -0.023). GPTQ-int8 on TRTLLM (CUDA15) has smaller delta ~ -0.008. So AWQ seems particularly sensitive.

ryan: makes sense. AWQ relies on per-token scale factors and folded biases; non-deterministic accumulation ordering in fused kernels amplifies noise. Action item: bisect TRTLLM kernel that changed between releases and create minimal repro that toggles fusion.

ml-ci-bot: action created: TKT-1127 — investigate TRTLLM fusion interaction with AWQ. Assigned to @ryan, priority P1.

maia: while we debug the runtime, workaround plan: 1) pin CUDA 14 + TRT 8.x for Dedicated clusters running AWQ-critical workloads 2) add a CI quant-bakeoff gating check that runs AWQ-int8 on a small eval set after driver or TRT upgrades 3) document `--tensorrt-force-legacy-kernels` env var for SRE runbooks.

alex: +1. I'll open a PR to add the gating job and the runbook snippet. Meanwhile I'll run a tighter repro to capture perf counters and nvprof traces.

sophia: if you get an nvprof/trt trace, dump the op ordering and we can try to simulate reordering in a Python reference to see expected numeric deltas.

ryan: also filing an upstream bug to TRTLLM team with fused-kernel trace and our AWQ quant table. cc @tensorrt-team if anyone here has contacts.

alex: for transparency — adding quick checklist in the ticket: CUDA version, driver microcode, TRTLLM commit hash, model config, quant params (per-channel scales), seed, eval set id.

maia: tiny note — for customers on Redwood Dedicated, we should offer an automated detection script that runs a short AWQ sanity test after driver updates and alerts if delta > 1%. Could be part of Redwood Optimize.

alex: agreed. ok team — next steps: ryan to bisect TRT kernel, sophia to validate workaround env vars on CI image, maia to draft runbook + gating job spec, alex to produce nvprof traces and push artifacts to the ticket. Meeting if needed after initial bisect. :eyes:

ryan: I'll kick off the bisect tomorrow morning and post interim findings here. :shipit:

sophia: thanks — will try the env var tests now and report within the hour. :coffee:
